lead: A code block: a header with the language (or a title) and a copy button, above scrollable code. It ships a lightweight highlighter and depends on no library like shiki; for more precise highlighting, plug in your own with `highlight`. Mostly used for fenced code in Markdown.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Built in: js / ts / json / python / bash / css / html / sql; an unrecognized language is plain text.

themes.title: Themes
themes.description: 8 popular themes built in: GitHub, One, Solarized and Catppuccin follow light / dark mode; Dracula, Nord, Monokai and Tokyo Night are always dark. They are independent of the theme style: switching the theme style keeps the code block's colors. Colors of the official palettes with a contrast below 4.5 have been nudged just enough to pass.

custom.title: Custom highlighter
custom.description: Pass a function to `highlight` that returns the highlighted content line by line (here it only bolds each line's first word; in practice, use something like shiki).

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.language: The language / title text in the header
styling.copy: Copy button; `data-copied` means a copy just succeeded (the icon becomes a check mark)
styling.status: The text announced after a copy (`role=status`, visually hidden)
styling.code: The code and each line (line numbers come from a CSS counter)
styling.token: A highlighted piece: keyword / string / comment / number / property / variable
